1696.title: Continuing Professional Development candidate
1696.content: Training that is beyond clinical update and includes wide-ranging competences like research and scientific writing; multidisciplinary context of patient care; professionalism and ethical practice; communication, leadership, management and behavioural skills; team building; information technology; auditing; and appropriate attitudinal change to ensure improved patient service, research outcomes, and attainment of the highest degree of satisfaction by stakeholders. The form of continuing professional development (CPD) may include: courses and lectures; training days; peer review; clinical audit; reading journals; attending conferences; e-learning activity. CPD may be included in national standards of conduct, performance and ethics that govern health workers. Also called: Continuing professional development . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 88; PDF page 102). 1776.doc: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution
1776.title: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution candidate
1776.content: An established institution that provides education as its main purpose, such as a school, college, university or training centre. Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. In practice, for international comparability, any educational institution not managed by a government institution is classified as private. Also called: Health workforce education and training institution . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). 1802.title: Remuneration candidate
1802.content: Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). 1816.title: Public Health Workforce candidate
1816.content: The public health workforce comprises all individuals who contribute to the delivery of at least one of the essential public health functions as part of integrated services and systems. This workforce comprises diverse and multidisciplinary occupations, from the health as well as other non-health sectors. This workforce can be conceptualized as three broad groupings: core group of public health personnel who have undergone professional training and/or registration with professional bodies in public health and could be from either health or another background; health and care workers who contribute to one or more public health functions as part of their clinical and/or social care roles; and personnel from a wide group of other allied occupations who contribute to addressing the determinants of health – for instance, personnel engaged in water and sanitation, food supply chains and road safety. Also called: Public health workforce . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). 2022.title: Facility Type candidate
2022.content: Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. Also called: Facility type . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 89; PDF page 103). 2037.title: Facility/Institution Ownership Type candidate
2037.content: Classification for ownership type: • Publicly-owned: Facilities owned or controlled by a governmental unit or a public corporation (where control is defined as the ability to determine the general corporate policy) corresponding to the institutional sector “government units” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • Not-for-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal or social entities created for the purpose of producing goods and services, whose status does not permit them to be a source of income, profit, or other financial gain for the unit(s) that establish, control or finance them, corresponding to the institutional sector “non-profit institutions serving households” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • For-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal entities set up for the purpose of producing goods and services and are capable of generating a profit or other financial gain for their owners corresponding to the institutional sector “non-financial corporations” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. Also called: Facility/institution ownership type . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). 2055.title: Gender candidate
2055.content: Gender refers to the characteristics of women, men, girls and boys that are socially constructed. This includes norms, behaviours and roles associated with being a woman, man, girl or boy, as well as relationships with each other. As a social construct, gender varies from society to society and can change over time. Gender is hierarchical and produces inequalities that intersect with other social and economic inequalities. Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. In practice, for international comparability, any educational institution not managed by a government institution is classified as private. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). 2074.title: F
2074.content: Facility Type candidate Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. 2075.content: Gender candidate Gender refers to the characteristics of women, men, girls and boys that are socially constructed. This includes norms, behaviours and roles associated with being a woman, man, girl or boy, as well as relationships with each other. As a social construct, gender varies from society to society and can change over time. Gender is hierarchical and produces inequalities that intersect with other social and economic inequalities. The handbook cites its reference 48 for this entry. | Facility Type (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. Public Health Workforce candidate The public health workforce comprises all individuals who contribute to the delivery of at least one of the essential public health functions as part of integrated services and systems. This workforce comprises diverse and multidisciplinary occupations, from the health as well as other non-health sectors. This workforce can be conceptualized as three broad groupings: core group of public health personnel who have undergone professional training and/or registration with professional bodies in public health and could be from either health or another background; health and care workers who contribute to one or more public health functions as part of their clinical and/or social care roles; and personnel from a wide group of other allied occupations who contribute to addressing the determinants of health – for instance, personnel engaged in water and sanitation, food supply chains and road safety. 2083.title: Q
2083.content: quality of the evidence In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout. Check a review log and its repository's issues for changes candidate, extracted The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet's Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository's open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check's. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell's old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet (Title the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue's URL; a closed issue's row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. Re-materialize and record new fixity candidate, extracted The gates are re-asked, not inherited: a licence can change, and a collection can grow past the size a caller agreed to. AND THE NEW FIXITY IS RECORDED IN THE SAME CHANGE. This step rewrites bytes that a materialization record describes, so leaving the old digest behind would make a CORRECT run of this process fail check:materialized-fixity as a mismatch — the gate reading "somebody edited held content without saying so" about the one process whose job is to replace it. This is the publication exception, stated as a rule rather than as a carve-out, because a list of permitted writers goes stale when a writer is added. The exception is NOT "these actors may skip the rule"; it is "say what you did". A writer that updates the digest alongside the bytes passes, and the record then describes what is actually there. A writer that does not fails, correctly, because it has forked upstream silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Apply . A re-pin commit therefore carries the new layers AND the surface rendered from them, because new layers shipped without their rendered surface fail the agent-memory tests. Work the source's categories of environmental change rather than free-associating: societal, governmental, economic, competitive, supplier and market changes, each item recorded with what it impacts. An opportunity is an external element that gives benefit; a threat is one that could cause trouble. Both are outside the subject and largely beyond its control — that is what puts them on this axis, not whether they feel good or bad. Its fourth section, markers, lists the content markers it found — sushi-config.yaml, a legacy dak.json, .bpmn processes, a beans store, library/, Lean, folio manifests — each with its paths, whether index.config.json already declares it (declared, not-declared, or unknown), and the snippet that would. bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/scan-repo-content.ts --json, a plain command any agent host can run. A strength gives advantage over others in the field; a weakness places the subject at a disadvantage relative to others. Both are attributes OF the subject. The source's warning belongs to this step specifically: listing strengths on paper "is very different from testing the organization and experiencing the strengths at work", so a strength recorded here is a claim, and where evidence for it exists it is cited. Sign the package and/or each asset candidate, extracted THE TRUST ANCHOR IS GDHCN, SPECIFIED BY THE WHO SMART TRUST IG. READ OFF THAT IG rather than from general knowledge: a GDHCN trustlist distributes KEY MATERIAL as W3C DID documents, and says nothing about what you wrap your bytes in — the health-certificate envelope is a separate specification in the same IG, and a document package is not a health certificate. So what is settled is where a verifier GETS THE KEY, not what it verifies. A portal that can fetch the bytes but not reach the trustlist cannot verify, which is unknown and not a failure — air-gapped is a declared deployment value, so that case is answered rather than assumed away. Still OPEN and unread: the rotation and revocation model, and whether a document-package signature can be expressed for a GDHCN-aware verifier at all. Two schemes with different properties remain to choose between, and the trustlist does not choose between them. A PACKAGE signature over the manifest verifies the SET — nothing added, removed or altered — and must be reissued whenever any file changes. A PER-ASSET signature verifies one file independently, which is what an edge cache serving one asset can actually check, and it cannot detect a removal because there is nothing left to verify. They compose; composing them is the safer and more expensive default, and it is the deployment's choice rather than the pipeline's. 2306.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, A–D
2306.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 365 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 244 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 205 terms and is 168 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 902 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 902 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 205 shown . 0–9 A B C D

2307.content: 1 · Declare in place (nothing moves) candidate, extracted A <name>.json entry with its graphs[] kinds. A sub-graph that owns its own layout gains a NESTED declaration whose paths resolve against its own directory, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Declare . 1 · Declare it in place, with its seam candidate, extracted <name>/<name>.json with name, version, repository (the planned home), livesAt (where it sits today), needs, and only the directories that exist, each declared with its files in one commit. <name>/platform.ts from the first commit, so no climb out of the directory ever needs rerouting. Scaffolded by init-folio --staged <path>, which writes those two files and nothing at the host root; never --instance, which writes a whole repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Declare . 1–3 · Declare, detangle, isolate candidate, extracted The graph-detanglement practice, all of its gates: declared in place, zero wrong-direction edges on every axis, and standing alone with its own declaration, namespace and artefact. A plain task on purpose, not a call to graph-detanglement.bpmn: that process ends in its own authorise-and-extract steps, which here are stages 9-13 of this one, and calling it would run them twice. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Detangle . 10 · Re-point: livesAt, seam, mount or subscription candidate, extracted In the new repository livesAt goes (absent means it sits at the root of repository) and platform.ts points at where the platform now is. The host consumes it as a remote mount (a source.remote instance in its root index.config.json) if it imports its code, or a subscription if it only reads its content, pinned to a commit while staging. Additive: the host keeps its copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Repoint . 10 · Seed both repositories candidate, extracted Seed main, then bring the content and the tools in as reviewed pull requests with their history, so neither repository's first commit is unreviewable. The seed includes every publisher the declaration promises (sub-kg-lifecycle stage 10): a qa directory with storage needs .github/workflows/publish-qa.yml, the caller of the tools layer's layer-qa-publish.yml, and test/results/ ignored. Without it the declared store is never written, and once the layer stops committing its results no reader finds them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Seed . 11 · Parent consumes, additively candidate, extracted The parent pins the pair (a commit while staging, a version once released) — a code dependency as a source.remote instance in its root index.config.json (remote-mount skill), never a submodule — repoints its imports, and keeps its own copy until it is green with the dependency declared. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Consume . 11 · Verify on a fresh clone candidate, extracted bun run cat sub-kg:verify-clone --repo <owner>/<name> --ref <branch> (Tool sub-kg-verify-clone): clone into an empty scratch directory with submodules and any sibling it needs, install, and run its own gates. Green, red or unknown, and unknown is never green. Nothing in a seed runs standalone until the seam is re-pointed, so a missing module shows here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_FreshClone . 12 · First release candidate, extracted Tag each repository, publish /v<major>/. From here the two are versioned independently; a tools release lists the content majors it supports. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Release . 12 · Owner confirms: freeze the in-repo copy candidate, extracted The agent reports the files that would move, their size, the new repository and the commit the copy matches, then asks: (1) freeze it in the kept trashcan now, (2) keep in place until the first release, (3) show the file list first. Default if there is no answer: (2), nothing moves. A green fresh clone is the precondition for asking, not the answer. Non-relaxable. The host keeps a FROZEN copy in the kept trashcan, not a refreshed mirror and not a deletion; the live copy is the remote mount or subscription set up at stage 10. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_ConfirmCutover . 13 · Cutover: freeze the copy in the kept trashcan candidate, extracted Only on the owner's answer (1) at step 12. The in-repo directory moves, as one relocation, under separated/<name>/ in the kept trashcan, on its own branch (a plain mv, git rm --cached, state:push; the trashcan skill says how), with ONE note carrying movedFrom, movedOn, the new repository and the commit the copy matches. Frozen: never refreshed, never rendered; a reader wanting the live content follows the note to the new repository. On main this is one revertable commit removing the directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Cutover . 13 · Cutover: retire the parent's copy candidate, extracted The one commit worth reverting, made only after the parent consumes the release and every identifier dereferences. It retires the parent's copy, frozen, never refreshed and never rendered, rather than deleting it. Where the copy goes is the sub-kg-lifecycle skill's stage 13; this diagram does not name that store, because the published graph must not. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Cutover . 2 · Grow it in place candidate, extracted The content type's own authoring process runs here, against the staged instance. Many sub-KGs never leave; this task can last as long as the graph does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Grow . 2a · Measure — unassigned column FIRST candidate, extracted bun run cat check:partition. Read the unassigned column before the edge count, and quote BOTH numbers rather than only the one that improved. The edge count can rise when the measurement improves (previously unjudged edges are folded in); that is correct. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Measure . 2b · Prune, merge, factor — or the classification is wrong candidate, extracted The only four moves. Move the shared TARGET first and the importers after; check the target's layer before the importer's; a schema moves with its script. The fix is never an exemption, it is the right owner. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Move . 3 · Isolate — own declaration, namespace, artefact candidate, extracted Only once cross-edges measure zero: give the sub-graph its own declaration, its own namespace and its own published artefact, as bootstrap/ has (its own declaration, bs: namespace and graph document). Nothing moves yet; the sub-graph now stands alone in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Isolate . 3 · Push generic down first candidate, extracted Move what is generic into the harness below before the seam is closed, and consolidate what the sub-KG needs into the harness it instantiates. Wrong-direction edges hide in declarations and data as well as imports: run check:import-direction, check:reference-direction and check:process-bindings. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_PushDown . 4 · Extract — a directory move, not a file-by-file sift candidate, extracted Only once edges are zero and the declaration stands alone: move the sub-graph out as one directory move, not a file-by-file sift. Its nested declaration resolves paths against its own directory, so moving the folder moves the graph. The five-point gate is in migration-plan.md Phase II. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Extract . 4 · Identity: version, iriBase, nodeSchemas candidate, extracted The declaration carries name, version, iriBase, needs and nodeSchemas. A base move is bun run iri:sync -- --from <old base>, once; then iri:sync:check and check:node-iris are green. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Identity . 4 · Route every climb through platform.ts candidate, extracted Every platform symbol the sub-KG uses is re-exported from <name>/platform.ts, so re-pointing the platform is a one-file edit. A merge from main is where new climbs arrive; reroute them here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Seam . 5 · Move harness output about it to the host candidate, extracted QA verdicts, translation templates, the exported graph and the glossary ledger are harness output ABOUT the graph: they live with the harness (kgQaHomeFor, translationsHomeFor). The content keeps only what its own checks need; the leak test's pending list is empty. The one exception is a separated layer that declares a qa directory of its own with storage: its verdicts are its own repository's, published to that repository's qa-reports branch (step 10), and read by a host at the commit it pins. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Hosted . 5 · Rehearse self-contained candidate, extracted bun run cat seed:ready --layer <name> --rehearse copies the layer and what it needs into a scratch workspace of sibling directories and runs the tests there. Run the gates rather than scanning imports: a static scan misses files the gates load at run time, and renaming the directory changes every generated page. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Rehearse . 6 · Report what would move, and how it undoes candidate, extracted Before the first outward-facing step the agent reports: the files and bytes that would move, the history that comes with them, what in the host changes, and how each step is undone. It never creates a repository on its own initiative. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Report . 6 · Split content from tools candidate, extracted Create <name>-tools as a sibling directory and move the code: the Zod source, the generators, the README and diagram writers, the content checks. Cut its import cone to its own files and declared packages. Both start at the content's version. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Split . 7 · Owner confirms: create the repository candidate, extracted Creating a repository is visible outside this one and is not undone by a revert. Numbered options, recommended first: (1) the owner creates it and says when it exists, (2) the agent creates it, only with that permission, (3) not yet. Default if there is no answer: (3), nothing is created. Non-relaxable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_ConfirmCreate . 7 · Plan publication candidate, extracted Every identifier the content mints is a file some step publishes: /v<major>/, for what programs read and pages people read alike; the exact release is the pin's. Name collisions between published files are resolved here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Plan . 8 · Create the repository candidate, extracted The owner creates the repository, or authorises the agent that has the permission to; when that agent is in another environment, the hand-over is one work item and one sentence (agent-handoff). The new repository is read before anything is written to it: empty is a fact to check, not to assume. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_CreateRepo . 8 · Rehearse standalone candidate, extracted Copy the content and the tools alone into a temporary directory, with nothing else on the path, and run the tools' checks there. An empty tree must exit non-zero, so a rehearsal over nothing cannot pass. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Rehearse . 9 · Authorise the extraction candidate, extracted A repository cut changes the substrate every other process binds to; that is a person's decision. Declining leaves the graph declared, detangled, isolated and split in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Authorise . 9 · Copy the staged contents in, with history candidate, extracted git subtree split --prefix=<name> in the host, then the split branch added to the new repository on a branch, as a draft pull request, never straight to main. The new repository's own root files are a second commit, so the copy stays byte-identical and reviewable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Seed .

2308.title: A
2308.content: Accept it, and record where it came from candidate, extracted Both branches land here. An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. Provenance is recorded whichever channel it arrived through: a description given in chat has a source and can be wrong, exactly as a PDF does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Accept . Accept the new state candidate, extracted Runs the check again with --accept, so the state file holds what was just handled and the next poll compares against it. A row the pass could not finish stays changed and is picked up on the next poll. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_Accept . Accept, or send back candidate, extracted The editor's lane, kept separate on purpose: the reviewer who judged the change is not the position that accepts it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Accessibility: measure, do not assert candidate, extracted Contrast COMPUTED against the real ground, including the worst case a backdrop can present; a non-colour channel wherever colour carries meaning (SC 1.4.1); an accessible name on every region; keyboard and focus order. An automated pass is necessary and not sufficient — axe accepts a non-empty placeholder as an accessible name, and a CSS selector that matches nothing raises no error at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Accessibility . Act on the answer candidate, extracted Never ask the person again for what they answered. A rule-level answer goes into the governing skill in the same turn. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Act . Add an actor, and declare its kind candidate, extracted Human, agentic or mechanical. A userTask because the agentic/mechanical line is JUDGEMENT — role-model.md says so — and reading it wrong disqualifies the actor from every judgement task it exists to perform, silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AddActor . Adjudicate the conflict candidate, extracted A human or agentic decision, never a merge rule. Which side wins depends on why the local edit was made, and a process that picked automatically would be choosing without the one fact that decides it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted adjudication.bpmn. When the editor and a reviewer, or two reviewers, disagree about a finding, an adjudicator settles it and records why; the review comment moves to adjudicated with the Decision that closed it. Permitted answers: stands — the finding is right and the author addresses it; withdrawn — the finding is wrong and the comment closes. Recorded on the comment, not branched: either way the flow goes on to the coverage check. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate the flagged passage candidate, extracted A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_FlagDrift . Adjudicate the flagged passage (human) candidate, extracted A human SME or editor reviews the flagged passage. They may: - Accept the translation as-is (false positive) - Edit the translation and re-run QA - Reject and request re-translation The round trip establishes that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the voice findings candidate, extracted Three outcomes, all legitimate: the register is wrong for this genre; the criterion does not belong in this genre and should carry profiles; or the block is a stated exception and a reviewer entry records why. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-narrative.bpmn#Task_AdjudicateVoice . Adjudicate: prose, scope, or exception candidate, extracted The same three outcomes as the base voice axis. The register is wrong for this block (fix the prose); the rule does not apply to this content (scope it on the voice, one edit rather than ten overrules); or the rule applies and this block is an exception (a reviewer entry saying why). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudication candidate, extracted folio-assistant's adjudication: the adjudication leads, the checker's entry is kept, and the dispensation carries its reason. Reviewers disagreeing on ONE criterion is a criterion disagreement, so this calls the QA-criterion specialisation: the failing entry stands, the criterion does not apply to this screen, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The entry condition matches exactly rather than approximately: GW_Agree asks whether the blind reviewers' entries agree and takes no here, and Process_CriterionAdjudication starts at "entries for one criterion disagree" — R_Review records pass, warn or fail PER CRITERION with a reason, so the disagreement reaching this step is a per-criterion disagreement between reviewer entries and nothing else. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Agent pass on the changed rows candidate, extracted For each changed row, the agent pass of Contributor feedback on a working draft: Ready for agent = Yes gets its edit, Ready for merge = Yes its merge, and a Blue answer to a Decision needed question is taken up. Every new row (from an issue, a person or a TWG workbook), every row with an empty Feedback (agent) and every row whose Blue cells changed gets feedback in the same wake, in the fixed layout: the ask first (Decision needed: with lettered options, one recommended, and where to answer), then Proposed direction: and Next:, only the tags bold. The work stays inside the row's Selected Sections; a row with none gets a question asking which, and any edit outside them is named on an Outside the selected sections: line. PRs are named as repo#n, which the sheet script links, and it adds a Where to review line linking each selected section on the preview. The agent then runs tools/review-log-watch/lint.ts and fixes what it flags: a cell that breaks the layout, or a PR state that GitHub contradicts. The agent records its step on the Agent tab at once, with the real time. Previews follow main: by default (Config PREVIEW_REFRESH automatic) the agent runs tools/review-log-watch/previews.ts on every poll for every open change-set PR, and also when people act on a change set (new Blue feedback, Ready for agent set to Yes, or feedback asking to update the preview); with PREVIEW_REFRESH on-feedback, only then. A branch behind main gets main merged in (a merge commit), pushed and restaged; a conflict a person must settle is asked in the change set's feedback. People agree the requirements there, and the committee or editor changes the record with cs-add / cs-remove / cs-title / cs-requirements / cs-committee / cs-merge / cs-split / cs-close / cs-new. Making change-sets is people's, in any of three ways, each like opening an issue: a row on the review sheet's Review Change Sets with only a Title (the sheet script gives it the next id), a change-set issue from the folio's change-set issue form, or feedback that says a change-set should be split, merged or moved. For the last two the agent proposes the change-sets and which comments go where, as a Decision needed question, and makes them only once an Editor sets Ready for agent to Yes. A comment is moved by typing another change-set's id, or new, in Change Set (human). The issue's change-set section is rendered from the record and put back if hand-edited; the nightly reconcile keeps every issue in line. The issue is for requirements; the PR that closes it is for preview, review and approval. Visibility is the whole point — without it a sibling session or a human cannot tell that work has begun, only that it has finished. Deliberately on this edge and not inside Phase 6. The three loops back into A_Implement (increment rejected, MVP not ready, feedback translated) re-enter implementation on the SAME branch, and re-announcing on each would be noise. Announce once, when the branch is created. Answer the other four gates candidate, extracted Restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, each answered permitted, refused or unknown. They are four answers to one decision, and Gateway_Gates reads them with size through decisions/materialization-gate.dmn. RESTRICTIONS. 'No restrictions known in context' is a STATE, not a green light. GateVerdict is three-valued for this reason alone, and unknown is never rendered as permitted. COPYRIGHT. What the licence permits for THIS bitstream, and separately whether it permits the derivation. LICENSE-CONTENT.md exists in this repository and the ingestion pipeline does not read it. RETENTION. A copy with no expiry cannot be told from an abandoned one — the same argument bean-blocking makes about a block with no expiry. An ARCHIVAL copy is the exception and it is a specification rather than an omission: freshness() reports it permanent, not no-expiry. SOURCE LOSS. Not hypothetical. The one IRIS record this repository holds carries a handle on iris.wpro.who.int, a regional instance merged into the global one. Only an ARCHIVAL copy of the original bytes discharges this; a working copy cannot, because the derived sections are not the publication. It goes through the same order as any question — say what you determined and what you could not, the candidates you see, the one you would pick and why — and it allows NO default: a Process or Role assumed rather than confirmed is an authority nobody gave. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_ArchiveReleaseBean . Close the change set: the issue, then the sheet row candidate, extracted Closing is one step with two tools, GitHub and the review sheet. The agent closes the change set's issue on GitHub, with the merge or the reason it closed unmerged, then records Agentic status Closed (or Change merged) on the Agent tab through Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn). The sheet script then hides the row and strikes the whole row through ("make sure complete changeset rows are hidden so not cluttered and that text of that whole row is crossed out"). The agent never hides or strikes a row by hand, and never deletes one: reopening the issue and writing a new status shows it again. Hiding and striking are formatting only, which the review-log watcher ignores. A change set closed without a merge, at a person's request, takes this step too. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_CloseReleaseBeans . Close the session candidate, extracted Records that the actor stopped. It does NOT resolve beans or complete instances: those outlive the session by design, and a machine that closed them on the way out would be asserting work finished because somebody went away. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_CloseSession . Close the tracking issue candidate, extracted Clean: close the open issue carrying the tracking label (the label input), if any, saying why the verdict is clean. Runs only on a clean verdict — on unknown the issue is left untouched and the job fails instead, because could-not-check is never rendered as clean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_CloseTrackingIssue . Never the other way round: an agent must never assume completion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Close . Code node review candidate, extracted Descend into Process_CodeReview. The actor takes on the code-reviewer lane for this call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_CodeReview . Cold start: mount and attach candidate, extracted Lay down every pinned layer from each instance's lock, as its AGENTS.md cold start says, and attach each repository the run will change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_ColdStart . Collate findings into a report candidate, extracted Mechanical results and review findings are merged into one report against the proposed change. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_CollateFindings . Comment staging URL on PR candidate, extracted Bot comments or updates the staging URL on the PR. Includes commit SHA, branch name, and build log link, and the review list of rendered files the change alters (skill rendered-impact), each linked on the preview and on main, with any input the renderer could not place named as not known. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-stage.bpmn#Task_CommentPR . Commit into the corpus candidate, extracted Only now does the change become corpus content, together with its QA sidecars. Subject to the commit-hygiene requirement. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_Commit . Commit, push, update PR candidate, extracted Agent commits all changes to the feature branch and pushes. The feature-staging.yml workflow automatically deploys to branches/<branch-slug>/ and comments the URL on the PR. For a rendered change the agent also produces the before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) and links it in the PR body. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_CommitPush . Compare main vs staging candidate, extracted The review starts from the Change Set's RENDERED list (skill rendered-impact): every rendered file the change alters, predicted from each renderer's dependency cone and checked against the build. The reviewer opens every content page on it, not only the pages the author mentions; index files are listed but not reviewed. An input the renderer could not place is shown as not known, never as no change. Review committee opens both URLs side by side: - Main site: <pages-url>/ (current published state) - Staging: <pages-url>/branches/<branch-slug>/ The staging banner shows the commit SHA so they can verify what they are reviewing matches the PR. A changed figure, diagram or table is also pictured before and after on the review page, with the share of changed pixels in words (skill visual-diff, Tool folio-block-screenshots). Anything the staging job cannot picture (page chrome, scroll behaviour, a PDF page, an IG page) is in the agent's before/after preview (skill before-after-preview). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Task_CompareBeforeAfter . Compare old, new and our adaptations candidate, extracted Attach the impact report to the re-pin: the changes that reach this site (only what it mounts), and its own files that look like adaptations of a changed file. The team adds what a diff cannot see: which policies, local decisions and translations rest on the changed text. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Impact . Compare what the processes need with what is granted candidate, extracted The needed set is the agent-permissions skill's list (write generated projections: CI only, never the agent; edit hooks or settings; run the gates; push a feature branch; open a PR), scoped to what this instance's processes actually call. The granted set is the recorded grants plus the Tool's current config, read through its adapter. A config rule with no recorded grant is reported as unrecorded, not treated as granted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/secure-agent-permissions.bpmn#Task_ReadGrants . Compose each harness's nav and tile candidate, extracted One themed section per instance in dependency order, from its declaration: its docs, its declared subgraphs (a graph with no viewer is shown inert and labelled), and its theme. Written to _data/harness.json by sync-docs-harness.ts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Tiles . Compose the full question candidate, extracted What is being decided, stated as what will differ; every id, path and coined name glossed; every option with its letter, a one-line explanation and its trade-off; the recommendation, first and marked; what will happen if no answer comes. Can the reader answer without opening anything? If not, it is not ready. More than one decision open: ask the next one in full and give a count for the rest. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/ask-the-person.bpmn#A_Compose . Compose the hand-back and post it in own thread candidate, extracted Compose it once, against the input schema: a question is the full ask-the-person input (what will differ, context, lettered options with a one-line trade-off each, the recommendation, what happens with no answer); context, a result or a blocker gets the same stand-alone test. Post it in your own thread too, chat text then card. Your own thread is never the only copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Compose . Compose the message candidate, extracted Five required strings — timestamp, actor, process, task, message — and one optional markdown body. The five are required because each answers a question a reader of the log will otherwise have to guess, and a guessed answer in a log is worse than a missing one. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/log-message.bpmn#A_Compose . Confirm all criteria met candidate, extracted The business analyst confirms every acceptance criterion from the requirements is met. The issue closes only on their authorisation — an agent never closes an issue on its own say-so. It IS an adjudication with the requirement-set answers: an approval here moves the set to accepted, which check:requirements refuses unless it is a human's and every approved member is in-force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#BA_Confirm . Confirm needs statement candidate, extracted Stakeholders confirm, on the issue, that the needs statement says what they need — or say what to change. A stakeholder's judgement; an agent does not record it for them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#S_ConfirmNeeds . Confirm the cardinalities candidate, extracted An operational question, asked of the people who run the process because they know where the exceptions are. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#S_ConfirmCardinality . Confirm the entities are the ones meant candidate, extracted A naming question. The BA owns the domain vocabulary; the agent does not guess, which is CRDM's own rule for phase 1 and applies here with more force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#BA_ConfirmEntities . Consolidate findings candidate, extracted One report from however many subprocesses ran. Findings are advice: a reviewer cannot accept the change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_Consolidate . Contributor feedback candidate, extracted Process_ContributorFeedback: while the document is a working draft, the Authoring Committee gives feedback through the Contributor Feedback sheet, and each change set is edited and merged in its own pull request. When its changes are merged, the document is validated and rendered again. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/folio-review-publish.bpmn#Call_ContributorFeedback . Copy asset into target folio and declare in assets[] candidate, extracted Write the asset bytes into a declared path inside the target folio and add the KgAsset entry to the target folio's <name>.json assets[] list (directory-conventions). Never drop the copy into an undeclared scratch directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/copy-into-folio.bpmn#Task_CopyAndDeclareAsset . Create feature branch candidate, extracted Agent creates a feature branch from main. Branch naming: feature/<short-description> Opens a PR immediately (AGENTS.md: "open the PR at the first commit"). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_CreateBranch . Create the repositories candidate, extracted The owner creates the content and tools repositories and their Pages. Nothing is committed to them before this. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Create . Create the repository candidate, extracted Only on the new-repo branch, and only after the user has named it. An empty working directory is scaffolded in place instead. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_CreateRepo . Cross the axes into SO, WO, ST, WT candidate, extracted The TOWS matching step, and the only step that produces anything actionable. Strengths and weaknesses across, opportunities and threats down, and each cell names the strategy the pairing implies: SO — achieve opportunities that greatly match the strengths; WO — overcome weaknesses to attain opportunities; ST — use strengths to reduce vulnerability to threats; WT — prevent weaknesses, to avoid becoming more susceptible to threats. A SWOT that stops at four lists is the failure the source names as its central one. This step is what the process exists to reach. It produces CANDIDATE strategies, not a chosen one, and they are not ranked — see the process documentation on why no scoring activity exists.
