3185.content: The skill review-comments as its source file folio-assistant-core/skills/content/content-lifecycle-ext/review-comments.md writes it, rendered by gen-processes-viz.ts because it has no instruction page on this site — do not edit here. All processes .

3186.title: Review heat map — where to look first
3186.content: Skill review-heatmap: The review page’s heat map: a section-by-metric table that tells a reviewer of a large document where to look first. Says what each column MEANS and what it must NOT be read as, where each number comes from, what a column says when a build lacks its data, and how the colour was chosen. Use when a reviewer or author asks “where do I start”, reads a number off the heat map, or asks why coverage or QA say “no data”; and before adding a column. Named by: Committee review of a content change, Draft, review and publish, Data sharing agreement document life cycle, Release a draft for public comment, Public comment on a review draft . Skill id: review-heatmap · Package: folio-core . The review page (review/ in a folio’s staging preview) opens with a table. It has one row per section, in reading order, and one column per measure. The darker a cell, the more there is. Every cell also shows its number, so colour never carries the meaning alone. A section’s name moves focus to that section in the list of changes below it. It is not the block-dependency heat map in content-graph. That one draws which blocks depend on which, for a paper’s structure; this one is about a REVIEW.

3187.title: What each column means, and must not be read as
3187.content: | column | counts | from | must NOT be read as | . | Changed blocks | blocks in the section that the ChangeSet lists: added, removed or changed | changeset.json | how much text changed. A one-word edit and a rewrite each count 1. | . | Open comments | review comments still open or addressed, with defects counted in brackets | review-comments.json | how bad the section is. One comment may be about the whole section, and a question is not a defect. | . | Stale comments | open comments whose block changed AFTER the comment was made (its recorded hash differs from the block’s current one) | review-comments.json + blocks.json | wrong or obsolete. It means re-read the block before replying, because the reviewer saw an earlier version. | . | Review coverage | “3 of 5 reviewed”: the section’s added or changed blocks, and how many have a reviewer VERDICT on their current version. Shaded by what is still unreviewed. | review-comments.json’s verdicts + blocks.json | “every comment is resolved”. Resolved comments are not a verdict: a question answered is not a block judged. A verdict on an earlier version is shown on the block and does NOT count, so an edit after review reopens exactly the blocks it touched. A file with no verdicts field reads “no data”, never “0 reviewed”. | . | QA | the section’s blocks whose latest QA verdicts FAIL (with the worst severity), and those whose verdicts are STALE or that were never audited | block-qa.json, published by the folio-block-qa-summary Tool after the staging job sweeps the build | a pass. A block counts as failing only on a verdict NEWER than the block; an older verdict makes it stale, and stale outranks passing. A section gets a row for QA alone only if something there fails or is stale. | . A column with no data says so in every row (“not published”, or “no data” when a build lacks the file). It is never 0 and never blank: zero reads as “measured, and nothing there”. Orphaned comments (their block is gone) have no section. They are counted in a last row, “(listed in no section)”, because an open comment is still open.

3188.title: Where the QA column’s data comes from
3188.content: The staging workflow first sweeps the build (its qa_sweep input, on by default), then runs the folio-block-qa-summary Tool (cat-harness-tools/scripts/publish-block-qa.ts). The Tool reads each block’s block-qa/v1 verdicts, runs no checker itself, and writes block-qa.json. So the column reports THIS build’s script-checkable criteria. Criteria that need an agent’s judgement are not run by the sweep. Each block is one of: . | failing: a fresh verdict failed; | stale: nothing fresh failed, but some verdict predates the block’s files; | passing: every latest verdict is fresh and none failed; | unaudited: no verdict at all. | . “Passing” says what was judged. Each block also carries needsAgent: its applicable criteria declared automated: false that have no fresh verdict. Which criteria count comes from each criterion’s own declaration, gated as the sweep gates it (applies_to, the folio’s active voices). The column then reads either: . | “N passing on scripts only (M criteria need an agent)”; or | “passing, every applicable criterion judged”. | . A summary without needsAgent reads “passing (this build does not say whether agent-judged criteria were run)”, never “all judged”: a verdict never given is not a pass. Freshness is the QA sweep’s own rule, including the uses-graph hash that graph-scoped criteria depend on; without it every graph-scoped criterion reads stale straight after a sweep. The QA sweep writes verdicts under the instance root; the summary also reads, second, under the directory the sweep was run on, so verdicts an older sweep wrote there are still found.

3189.title: How the colour was chosen
3189.content: This follows the dataviz skill: . | Scale. One hue (blue), sequential, in three ordinal steps. Each column is scaled to its own maximum, by thirds; zero has no fill. | Light theme: steps 250 / 400 / 550. | Dark theme: steps 600 / 500 / 400, chosen for the dark surface rather than flipped from the light ones. | Validation. Both ramps pass validate_palette.js --ordinal: they are monotone, their steps are visibly apart, and the lightest clears 2:1 against the surface. | Ink. Every cell’s text colour clears 4.7:1 against its fill. | . The table is a real <table> with row and column headers, so it is its own table view for a screen reader. Every cell also has a hover title saying what it counts.

3190.title: Where it lives
3190.content: . | cat-harness-tools/scripts/review-heat.ts: computeHeat (the numbers), heatBucket (the thirds) and renderHeat (the table). The page embeds all three with toString(), so the tested functions are the ones that run. | blocks.json carries each block’s section, so a comment on an UNCHANGED block still lands in its section’s row. | .

3193.title: Review-log watch
3193.content: Skill review-log-watch: Poll a review log (a drafting Contributor Feedback sheet, or a public-comment sheet’s Review Change Sets) and its folio repository’s issues mechanically, with Tool review-log-watch, and start agent work only when a cell people set or an open issue changed. Each issue that no row links yet becomes a Contributor Feedback row, and a closed issue’s row is hidden with its text struck through. Use on every wake of a review-log watcher, and when setting up a watcher for a new log. Named by: Record agent step, Review-log watch . A review log is a drafting or public-comment sheet (skill review-sheet-script) for one folio repository. The steps below are for a drafting log; a public-comment log differs as set out in “Public-comment logs”. A watcher is the agent thread that keeps it moving. This skill is what the watcher does on each wake. Process: processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn (checklist beside it).

3194.title: Why mechanical
3194.content: The watcher runs a core tool on every poll, and each issue gets a row on Contributor Feedback, including existing issues; a closed issue’s row is hidden, its text struck through. The poll wakes the watcher thread every minute. Until the tool says changed, the watcher only reads, runs the tool and does the stall pass (“Every poll”, below). It does not otherwise reason about the rows.

3195.title: Each wake
3195.content: . | Read two small ranges: . | Watch!F1:I1, where the sheet script writes Cells hash, the hash itself, and the time it last checked. The script rewrites it on every refresh and every timer tick, from the cells people set. | Contributor Feedback’s header row with its Change-set and Issue columns (A to K), so the tool can give a new row the next Change-set id. | . Save the values as JSON, with the header row and with an empty first row for each sheet row above it, so the row numbers stay the sheet’s. A sheet whose script has no Watch tab yet is read whole, from row 1, and gets no --sheet-hash. | Check: . bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch/watch.ts \ --repo litlfred/dth-phc --sheet values.json \ --state ~/.cache/review-log-watch/<sheet-id>.json \ --sheet-hash <Watch!G1> . | Exit 0 is {"status":"unchanged"}. Do the stall pass (below), then stop. The next wake was queued first. | Exit 10 is changed. The output has changes (an issue opened, updated or closed, or a cell’s old and new text) and append. | . Inserted rows. People may insert a row anywhere. The state keys each cell by its row’s Change-set id (CS-004:Ready for agent), and by sheet row only for a row with no id, so an insert moves no change set and reports nothing. A cell change carries cs and the row it is on now. Every row number in the output (changes[].row, closedRows) is from this read, so write only from the read you just checked, never from a row number kept from an earlier check. | Append each append[].row below the last row of Contributor Feedback. The row is already lined up with the header: . | Change-set: the next id, also in append[].agent.csId. | Title: the issue’s title. | First Contributor Feedback column: @login (#N): first paragraph. | Issue: the issue’s URL. | . The issue’s Markdown is turned into plain cell text: a [label](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/blob/main/skills/content/folio-document-adapter/url) shows its label, and bold, italic and code marks are dropped. Its links are in append[].links (the column and each link’s start, end and URL). Write the cell with those as textFormatRuns (updateCells), so each link is clickable. Then write append[].agent to the Agent tab as a new row: its Change-set and Issue columns. The script fills Contributor Feedback’s Issue column from the Agent tab, by Change-set, on every refresh, so an Issue written only on Contributor Feedback is cleared on the next refresh. Every other cell stays empty. This tool is the only thing that adds issue rows, so nobody adds them by hand. A row with closed: true is appended like the others and then treated as in step 4. | Closed issues. Hide each row in closedRows, plus the rows just appended for closed issues, and strike its text through. Hiding and striking are formatting only, so the row’s text and history stay. A reopened issue’s row is shown again, without the strike-through, by hand. | Agent pass. Run Contributor feedback on each changed row, and record the step on the Agent tab at once. A Ready for agent = Yes gets its edit, and a Ready for merge = Yes gets its merge. A Blue answer to a Decision needed question is taken up. Feedback on every Blue change and every new row. In every log the watcher keeps, the agent writes or rewrites Feedback (agent), in the layout of review-sheet-script (“The agent’s feedback cell has a fixed layout”), for each row that: . | is new, however it got there: from a GitHub issue (step 3), typed by a person, or copied from a TWG workbook; | has an empty Feedback (agent) cell; or | has Blue cells (Title, Selected Sections, any Contributor Feedback column, Disposition) that no longer match the Agent tab’s Feedback basis (feedbackBasis()), which is when the script shows “⚠ Stale”. It does this in the same wake, before accepting the state. A row it cannot finish keeps its stale mark and comes back on the next wake. The digest covers every row, not only issue rows, so a row with no issue still wakes the watcher. | . | Accept. Run the check again with the same inputs plus --accept, so the state file records what was handled. A row the pass could not finish still differs from the stored state, so it comes back on the next wake. | Queue the next wake. | .

3196.title: Every poll: hand new feedback on, and catch stalled rows
3196.content: New feedback goes to the agent working the row, and a stalled row is restarted or taken over; otherwise a contributor’s note can reach no one. This pass runs on every poll, changed or not, after the check: . | New feedback goes to the row’s agent. For each row whose Blue cells changed, find the thread that owns it: the one named in its Agent row or its Feedback (agent) cell, or else ask the coordinator. Send it the new text verbatim, with the CS id, the cell and the time. Then write in Feedback (agent) who has it and what happens next, so the contributor sees at once that it was heard. | Find stalled rows. A row is stalled when . | its Blue cells changed, or Ready for agent turned Yes, more than 10 minutes ago, and no Agent step has been recorded since; or | its agent has recorded no step for 2 hours while the row is open. | . | Restart or take over. Ask the owning thread once. If it gives no answer within 10 minutes, or it is done or stopped, take the row over yourself, or ask the coordinator for a new thread. Either way, write the new owner, its current step and a link into Feedback (agent). | . A row whose agent is working, but that shows nothing new, is not stalled: say what it is doing in Feedback (agent), with links to its pull requests, so the row stops looking stuck.

3197.title: Every poll: check each row against its Agent row
3197.content: After the stall pass, the watcher checks, for every row with a Feedback (agent) cell: . | a pull request or preview named in Feedback (agent) is the one in the row’s Agent row (Pull request, Staging review page); | Agent step reads <step> <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MMZ>, not prose; | Agentic status shows no “no agent has picked this up” warning while the row’s thread is working. | . A row that fails is fixed through Record agent step (processes/content/record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent row first, then Feedback (agent), then a read-back. Another thread that owns the row sends the watcher its step and links; the watcher writes them, because one watcher owns each log.

3198.title: Finished rows: hidden and struck through, and not feedback
3198.content: A finished change set’s row (Agentic status Change merged or Closed) is hidden and its whole row struck through by the sheet script. Watchers ignore that visual change: the check compares cell values only, so hiding, unhiding and the line are never a change, and a hidden row still counts as a row: never append it again. When the check lists closedRows (rows linking a closed issue), the watcher closes each through Record agent step with Agentic status Closed; the script does the hiding.

3199.title: What counts as a change
3199.content: . | Issues: the repository’s issues, open and closed, with their state and updated_at. --author <login> keeps only the issues one person opened. | Pull requests are left out. | So are issues labelled no-sheet, which an Editor sets to keep an issue off the sheet. | . | Cells: with --sheet-hash, the script’s hash stands for them, and a change shows as one change on #hash; the watcher then reads the rows to see which changed. Without it, the tool compares the cells itself. Either way, only the cells people set count, under these headers: . | Title, Selected Sections, every Contributor Feedback column, Disposition and Change Set (human) (Blue); | Ready for agent, Ready for merge and Dispositions confirmed (Orange); | on a public-comment log also every Committee Feedback column, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human). | . The agent’s Green columns and the script’s Grey ones are not watched, so the watcher’s own writes never wake it. | First check (baseline: true): with no state file yet, every issue counts as new and every unlinked issue gets a row. This is how an existing sheet takes in its existing issues. The watcher appends the rows, hides the closed ones and accepts, but starts no agent pass, because a cell that is merely seen for the first time has not changed. | .

3200.title: Setting up a watcher
3200.content: A log is not set up until a watcher has both of these wakes: . | a chain of 1-minute delayed wakes (send_later), each of which queues the next before it reads anything, so no poll is skipped during long work. A send_later fires once, so a wake that does not queue the next ends the chain; | an hourly scheduled task that restarts the chain if it breaks. | . Keep the state file outside the repository, one per sheet. Without it, a fresh container treats its first check as a first check: it reports every issue as opened, and appends rows only for issues that no row links yet.

3201.title: Limits
3201.content: . | The tool reads one tab and one repository, from the issues API (up to 100 issues a page, every page). It never writes the sheet or GitHub. | The summary is the issue’s first paragraph, cut to 300 characters. A link the cut runs through keeps its target on the part that is left. Committee members may rewrite the Title and their own column. | .

3209.title: Narrative review
3209.content: Process_NarrativeReview · advisory · 5 step(s) . Judging changed PROSE: read what the mechanical checkers flagged, decide which findings are real, then look at the two things no checker can judge — whether the editorial dependencies still hold and whether a translation still says what the source does. You are in this process when prose changed. review-code is its sibling for code nodes and review-task is what dispatches to either, so arriving here means somebody has already decided the change is narrative. Everything this lane produces is ADVICE. The reviewer records findings; accepting or refusing the change belongs to the editor’s lane in review-task, so a review can be thorough without being a veto. i i i i i

3215.title: Keep the review sheet’s Agent columns current
3215.content: Skill review-sheet-agent-columns: Whenever an agent works on a change set of a folio whose review sheet is kept by the Tool review-sheet-sync, it writes the Agent tabs’ columns for that change set and its comments as it goes: status, step, what it did, the PR, the staging page and its build, what the PR changed and when it finished. Use on every change-set edit, draft, PR, push, merge or close, in a sheet sync or not. Named by: Contributor feedback on a working draft, Record agent step, Review-log watch . When an agent works on a change set of a sheet that has the Tool enabled, it updates the Agent columns as part of the process. The sheet’s views (Agentic status, Staging review and the ⏳ line on Review Public Comments and Review Change Sets, or on Contributor Feedback in a drafting sheet) are built from the Agent tabs, so a change set worked without writing them shows reviewers nothing, or something old as current. The tabs, their columns and who writes each are the public-comment skill’s (§”The live review sheet”) and, for a drafting sheet, review-sheet-script §”Drafting mode”. How the script reads them, and the tool that makes the cells, are review-sheet-script’s (“Stale staging previews”, “Checked by commit”, “Writing the Agent tab with the tool”, “Where the agent is”). This skill says when the agent writes and what.

3216.title: When it applies
3216.content: The folio has the Tool enabled: it carries the Tool’s config, review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json (a drafting sheet: review/drafting/sheet-sync.json), and the session can reach the sheet through a Google Sheets connector. The sheet’s id is not in the repository; it is given by the project (its scheduled sheet-sync task, or the owner). It applies to any work on a change set, however it started: a sheet sync, a card, a thread message, an issue or a review comment on the PR. If the Tool is enabled but the sheet cannot be reached, do the work, and say in the reply that the sheet was not updated and why.

3217.title: The tabs
3217.content: . | Agent - Comments (public comment only): one row per comment (No.), with Agentic status, Agentic action taken, Agentic applied in, Agentic handled by, Agentic date actioned and Change-sets. | Agent - Change Sets (a drafting sheet: Agent): one row per change set, with Pull request, Staging review page, What the PRs changed, Agent completed, Feedback basis, Staging built, PR head, Staging built from, Staging deploy and Agent step (each header ends “(change set)”). | . A public-comment sheet may instead have one Agent tab (comments left, change sets right, the Config’s AGENT_CS empty). Write it the same way, by header.

3218.title: When to write
3218.content: One move, one Record agent step. Every move in the table below is the subprocess processes/content/record-agent-step.bpmn, in this order: . | Write the change set’s Agent row: Agentic status, Pull request, Staging review page, the build columns, and Agent step. | Write Feedback (agent) from that row, linking the same pull request and preview. | Read back Agentic status, Agentic status (filter) and Staging review after the script’s next run. If they disagree with Feedback (agent), fix the Agent row, never the copied columns. | . A preview link goes in only when it is live, so a reader never gets a . | Live means the GitHub Pages deploy of a gh-pages commit at or after the preview’s publish succeeded (pages-build-deployment run, conclusion success), and an HTTP GET of each link answers 200 where the agent can reach the site. A publish that is only on the gh-pages branch is not live: deploys queue, and the next push cancels a queued one. Until then leave Staging review page empty, set Staging deploy to deploying, and write “Preview deploying” in Feedback (agent) with no preview link. Link the pull request instead. | . How to tell it is live, from where the agent runs (agents can be firewalled from github.io): gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/workflows/pages-build-deployment/runs and take the newest run whose gh-pages commit is at or after the preview’s publish; completed with success is live, queued, in_progress or cancelled is not. Then write deployed in Staging deploy. The sheet script does not fetch pages (it has no network permission, by its security review); it shows the link only when Staging deploy says deployed. Never write Feedback (agent) alone. The script builds Agentic status and Staging review only from the Agent tab, so a preview link written only in Feedback (agent) leaves Staging review empty and Agentic status naming the old pull request (CS-007, 2026-11-01). Agent step must be exactly <step> <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MMZ> with a step from the fixed list; prose there is not read, and the row then warns “no agent has picked this up” however much work was done. A row waiting for people is idle <time>. Write as each step completes, not once at the end. Times, heads and steps come from bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/agent-record.ts, never typed. | step | per comment (Agent - Comments) | per change set (Agent - Change Sets) | . | work starts | Agentic status Working | Agent step reading (agent-record.ts step reading) | . | proposing, editing |   | Agent step proposing or editing | . | PR opened, or a push to it | PR open; action taken, applied in, handled by, date actioned | Pull request, Staging review page, What the PRs changed; PR head, Staging deploy and Agent completed from agent-record.ts push; Agent step pushing | . | preview on gh-pages, then live |   | Staging built from, Staging built; Staging deploy pushed, deploying, deployed; Agent step staging, deploying | . | Ready for agent acted on, no new commit | date actioned | Agent completed from agent-record.ts done | . | blocked on a decision | Needs human, and what is needed in action taken | Agent step idle | . | ready for review | Ready for review | Agent completed; Agent step qa-review or idle | . | merged | Change merged | clear the Staging review page (a merged branch’s preview 404s); Agent step idle; then close the change set (below) | . | closed unmerged | Not started, and say so in action taken | remove that PR’s line from Pull request, What the PRs changed, Agent completed and PR head; Agent step idle | . Adding change sets: write the Agent tab only (2026-11-01). On a public-comment log, Review Change Sets columns A:B (Change-set, Title) are a spill, =FILTER('Agent - Change Sets'!A3:B, ...) in A3, so a new change set is a new row at the end of Agent - Change Sets and nothing else. A value typed into Review Change Sets A:B blocks the spill: every id shows #REF! and the tab looks empty (the 82 DPI-H rows written to A210:B291 did this until they were cleared). Before writing any cell, read its formula; never write over or below a formula’s spill range. Closing a change set is one step with two tools, GitHub and the review sheet. Task Task_CloseChangeSet of processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn: close the GitHub issue (with the merge, or the reason it closed unmerged), then set the Agent row’s Agentic status to Closed (or Change merged) through Record agent step. The sheet script hides that row and strikes the whole row through; reopening the issue and writing a new status shows it again. Never hide, strike or delete a row by hand. A disposition for the change set is written only from agent-record.ts dispositions (review-sheet-script, “Writing the Agent tab with the tool”). New feedback while you work, and stalls. The log watcher (skill review-log-watch, “Every poll”) sends new Blue feedback on your row to you, verbatim. Answer it in the same turn: record the Agent step (reading at least), and tell the watcher your step and links, so the row shows who has it. Record a step at least every time you finish one: a row with no new step 10 minutes after its feedback changed, or none for 2 hours, counts as stalled, and the watcher restarts it or takes it over. Name your thread in the row’s Feedback (agent) so the watcher knows whom to ask.

3219.title: What to write
3219.content: . | Re-read the headers first. People move columns. Find each column by its header, never by a letter remembered from an earlier run. | Write only the Agent tabs. Every other tab is people’s, or formulas, or the Apps Script’s. The exceptions are the agent’s own Green feedback column (review-sheet-script) and an explicit instruction from the owner for a named cell. | Per comment (every PC in the change set): Agentic status; Agentic action taken (what was done, in a sentence); Agentic applied in (the sections or blocks changed); Agentic handled by (the agent and its session); Agentic date actioned (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MMZ, UTC, from the clock). | Per change set: Pull request (one PR URL per line); Staging review page (branches/<slug>/en/review/ while the PR is open); What the PRs changed (one line per PR, in the same order as the URLs: what that PR changes in the document, in a reader’s words); Agent completed and PR head (one line per PR, same order). A change set may have several PRs, and a line in any per-PR column always matches the line of its URL in Pull request. | Staging built and Staging built from: when, and from which commit, the preview was last built, read from the newest gh-pages commit under branches/<slug>/. Write them on every rebuild. The script compares them with Agent completed and PR head and flags a preview built before the last push as stale. | Agent step: write idle (or the next step) before leaving a change set. A step left behind shows “no update for N min” on the sheet. | Append, never reorder. A change set new to the tab goes at the end. Review Change Sets’ typed columns sit beside rows derived from it, so moving a row moves people’s inputs onto the wrong change set. | No reviewer names or emails anywhere the agent writes, in the sheet or in the repository. Name feedback by tab, row and column header. | Only a PR that edits the document for the change set goes in Pull request (public-comment §”Which PR counts”). | .

3220.title: Checking it
3220.content: After writing, read the change set’s row on Review Change Sets (or Contributor Feedback) back. Once the Apps Script has refreshed (its timer runs every minute), its Agentic status shows <repo>#n (status, completed) · what it changed for each PR, and Staging review shows no ⚠ unless the preview really is behind. A missing or wrong line there means an Agent cell is missing or out of step.

3221.title: review-sheet-agent-columns (skill)
3221.content: The skill review-sheet-agent-columns as its source file folio-assistant-core/skills/content/folio-document-adapter/review-sheet-agent-columns.md writes it, rendered by gen-processes-viz.ts because it has no instruction page on this site — do not edit here. All processes .

3222.title: The review sheet’s Apps Script
3222.content: Skill review-sheet-script: Build, install and reuse the Google Apps Script that keeps a review sheet’s links and joined columns current (Tool review-sheet-sync). Public-comment mode: comment numbers, sections, pages and lines link into the frozen review draft, and Review Change Sets joins its comments. Drafting mode: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set with its own GitHub issue, and Sections pick from the document’s table of contents. Use when setting up either sheet for a document, when its links are missing or stale, or after a tab, header, anchor or draft link changes. Named by: Contributor feedback on a working draft, Review and publish a folio, Guideline Updates, Release a draft for public comment, Record agent step, Review-log watch . The sheet itself, its tabs and who writes each column are the public-comment skill’s (§”The live review sheet”). This skill is the script that keeps that sheet’s links current, and the Tool review-sheet-sync that builds it. Links inside a cell’s text (a section, a page, a “No. n” in a joined column) cannot come from a formula, which makes at most one link per cell. They are rich text, which goes stale when the sheet changes, so a Google Apps Script bound to the sheet keeps them. Never paste them by hand from an agent: the next edit undoes it.

3223.title: Inputs and outputs
3223.content: Every actor on a review sheet reads and writes only what this table says. Columns are named by header, never by letter. “People’s tab” is Contributor Feedback (drafting) or Review Public Comments and Review Change Sets (public comment). | actor | reads | writes | never writes | . | People (Authoring Committee, Feedback Review Committee) | the whole sheet | Blue columns on the people’s tabs; cell comments | Green, Grey, Orange, Agent tabs, Config | . | Editor (the Config EDITORS list) | the whole sheet | Orange Ready for agent, Ready for merge | Green, Grey, Agent tabs, Config | . | Owner | the whole sheet | Config EDITORS | anything the agent or script writes | . | Apps Script (review-sheet.gs, built by Tool review-sheet-sync) | Config (CFG, COLS, DATA, EDITORS); the people’s tabs; the Agent tab(s) | Grey columns (ids, links, joins); Green columns copied from the Agent tab(s); the STALE mark on the agent column; Ready for agent back to No once, on the turn to stale; the Watch tab; protections on the Ready columns; the QC problems at the top of Disposition (agent) | Blue columns’ contents; Orange except the stale reset; the Agent tab(s) | . | Agent (sync or watcher) | the whole sheet, and above all the people’s Blue Disposition of each comment, which its dispositions start from; the folio’s repository | the Agent tab(s) (one row per change set, and in public comment one row per comment on Agent - Comments), including Disposition (change set) in the format below; the agent column, Feedback (agent) (drafting) or Change Set Feedback (agent) (public comment); Config rows other than EDITORS | Blue, Orange, Grey; the Title (on both kinds of sheet); Change Set (human) | . | QA reviewer (independent: an agent session that did not write the PR, or a person) | the change set’s Disposition (change set), the people’s Blue Disposition and feedback, the PR’s diff at its head commit, the staging QA report | QA gate (change set) and QA report (change set) on the Agent tab, nothing else | everything else, and never a change set whose PR it wrote | . | Tool review-sheet-sync | the folio’s review/*/sheet-sync.json, anchors, line map | Code.gs (generic); the Config rows for one sheet (--config ... --out rows); a drafting sheet’s TOC rows (--toc-out rows) | the sheet itself | . | Script review-anchors-from-folio.ts | the folio’s document manifests and block prose; optionally the library file it was seeded from | folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json (--check compares) | the sheet | . A question to people goes in the sheet, not only in chat. The agent’s feedback cell has a fixed layout. The agent writes, in this order and nothing else: . Decision needed: <one question, in plain words, naming what it is about> A. <option> (recommended) B. <option> Answer in your feedback column, then an Editor sets Ready for agent to Yes. Proposed direction: <what the agent proposes or did, in one to three lines> Next: <what happens next, and who does it> . | The ask comes first. Leave the Decision needed block out when nothing is asked; the cell then opens with Proposed direction:, and the script puts a “Please review: do you agree with the proposed direction below?” ask on its status line. | One option says (recommended); options are lettered so people answer with one letter. | Tags (Decision needed:, Proposed direction:, Next: and other line-start labels) are the only bold text, in black. The script bolds them; never write Markdown **. | Say only what stands now. History (“Step 2”, “Already done”, “Decided (Q1 …)”) goes to Disposition (agent), never here. Pull request state comes from the script’s ⏳ line, so the agent does not restate it. | At most 10 lines, so the row shows it whole. | Name pull requests and issues as repo#n (e.g. dth-hrh#82). The script links each one, and under its ⏳ line adds ↳ Where to review:, one link per Selected Section to that section on the change set’s preview (or on the published draft while there is no preview). The agent writes no URLs of its own for these. | . Selected Sections bound the work. The agent reads the row’s Selected Sections before it proposes anything, and its proposal, its edits and its PR stay inside them. A row with no section picked gets a Decision needed: question asking which sections (with the agent’s guess as the recommended option), or, for a row from an issue that names its block, the agent fills them in from the issue. When an edit must reach outside them (a glossary term, a figure in another chapter), the cell says so on its own line: Outside the selected sections: <which, and why>. The watcher checks every row against this layout on each poll (tools/review-log-watch/lint.ts, skill review-log-watch) and fixes any cell it flags. The lint also fails a row with feedback and no section picked, and a row whose PR changes a chapter none of its sections are in without the Outside the selected sections: line. When the agent needs a person to decide something about a change set, it writes the Decision needed block into that row’s agent column and sets the row’s Agentic status to Needs human on the Agent tab. The sheet never shows those words: Agentic status opens with Needs you: answer the agent’s question, and Agentic status (filter) reads Needs you: answer the agent's question, so the “Needs you” filter view finds it. The ⏳ line says “Needs you” only when the cell holds a Decision needed block; with none it says the question is missing. A card in the agent’s chat may carry the same question, but the sheet is the record people see. When the question is answered, the agent removes the block from the feedback and adds the decision, with who made it, to Disposition (agent). Disposition (agent): the change set’s decisions and dispositions. The agent keeps one record per change set in the Agent tab’s Disposition (change set), and the script shows it, read-only, in the Green Disposition (agent) column, just right of Ready for merge, on Review Change Sets or Contributor Feedback. An empty one reads, in bold, ⚠ No disposition yet for Nos. 127 to 131 and 134 when the change set has comments. It holds: . | The decision history, oldest first, one line per decision, never removed or rewritten: Decided (Q1, 2026-10-31): A, by the Editor; <what it means>. Change Set Feedback (agent) holds only the current proposal and any open question. | One disposition per comment, after an optional overall statement for the whole change set: . Overall: <a statement for the whole change set> No. 136: Accepted. DPI-F defined at first use, with a glossary entry. Nos. 127 to 135, 138 and 139: Not accepted. Already addressed. No. 326: Partially accepted. <what was done, and what was not> . A disposition is one of Accepted, Partially accepted, Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate, Out of scope or Withdrawn, first after the colon. Every comment of the change set gets exactly one. The script checks this (dispositionProblems) and puts any problem, in bold, at the top of Disposition (agent): ⚠ No disposition yet for No. 140, 141, ⚠ No. 9 is not in this change set, ⚠ No. 136 has two dispositions, or a line whose word is not a disposition. It never edits the Agent tab. Drawn from the people’s dispositions. Before writing a comment’s line, the agent reads that comment’s Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments (drafting: the row’s Blue Disposition). Where a person has set one, the line uses the same word; where it is empty or Pending, the agent proposes one. A word that differs from the people’s is flagged (⚠ No. 136: Accepted here, Noted in the people's Disposition) for the committee to settle, and never corrected by the agent or the script. The record is written before the staging preview is made, and kept current with each push. | . Once an Editor sets Ready for merge to Yes, the record as it stands is the summary: the agent puts it in the merge commit and posts it as the closing comment on the change set’s issue. From a sibling agent. An agent that is not the one talking with the owner, such as a project thread or a subagent, also writes its question here when the sheet governs the work. It is the review-sheet channel of the harness skill hand-back-to-discussion (cat-harness schemas/skills/hand-back-to-discussion/input.schema.json): . | channel field | on the sheet | . | spreadsheetId | the sheet, as the folio’s review/*/sheet-sync.json names it | . | tab | Review Change Sets, or Contributor Feedback on a drafting sheet | . | row | the change set id or comment number, never a row index | . | column | Change Set Feedback (agent) or Feedback (agent), by header | . The block, the Agentic status and the replacement on answer are the same as above. The sheet is an extra copy, never the only one: the sibling still hands the question back to the discussion agent, which asks the owner. A Blue-column answer counts as the answer in either place. The agent that takes it routes it to the other copy and marks that copy answered (the chat copy is struck through, with [Edit: …] added). What it keeps current. Columns are found by header text, so people may move them. | tab | column | becomes | . | Review Public Comments | No. | a link to the comment’s page (commentUrl + its ref from Agent’s Comment ref) | . | Review Public Comments | Sections | each section number, appendix, named section or chapter links to its first page in the draft | . | Review Public Comments | Page | each printed page or range links to that page | . | Review Public Comments | Agentic status | one line per pull request of the PC’s change-sets (Agent’s Pull request (change set)), <repo>#n (status, completed) · what it changed (the repository in the link text, because Sheets’ link popup cuts the URL short): the PR linked; the PC’s Agentic status and the matching line of Agent completed (UTC, change set) in bold; then the matching line of What the PRs changed (change set). A PC in several change-sets lists all of their PRs, each once. With no PR, the status alone | . | Review Public Comments | Line no(s) / Table / Figure | each p.N and each line(s) N–M / L N links to its page. Draft line numbers restart, so a line is placed on the page, near the row’s own pages, whose numbered lines hold it | . | Review Change Sets | Sections, Pages | the union over the change-set’s comments, sorted by page, each linked | . | Review Change Sets | Agentic status | the same, per change-set; the status is its PCs’ Agentic statuses, each once | . | Review Change Sets | Agentic status (filter) | one plain value per change set, for a filter view: “Needs you: answer the agent’s question” if any of its comments needs a person, else the least advanced of its comments’ Agentic statuses (Not started, Working, PR open, Ready for review, Change merged); “Not in comment record” only when all are | . | Review Change Sets | Public Comments | No. n (Status) · comment, status in bold, joined by a blank line | . | Review Change Sets | Suggested Revisions, PC Committee Feedback, Dispositions | No. n · text, one per comment | . Change Set Feedback (agent) (Review Change Sets, green, right of Ready for merge). The agent writes its proposed direction for resolving the change set here, and any question for people (§”Inputs and outputs”). The script only marks it stale. It is a proposal, never a person’s feedback: a tool that collects the people’s Committee Feedback (…) columns by header must leave it out, or show it apart, and it decides nothing. Column names live in Config COLS (rcs.agentFeedback, draft.agentFeedback). The script finds each column under any of its names (aliasOf, SAME_COLUMN), including the earlier Architect Feedback …, Architect Feedback (agent) and Contributor Feedback (agent), and a feedback basis written under those still matches. Every No. n in Review Change Sets links to #gid=<Review Public Comments>&range=A<row>. Do not link to a named range by #rangeid=: Sheets shows “Invalid range” for a named range whose id was set through the API. One script, one Config tab per sheet. Code.gs is the same file for every document: review-sheet.gs, stamped with its commit and made plain ASCII. Nothing about a document is in it. What differs per document lives in the sheet’s Config tab: visible, locked to the sheet’s owner, columns Key and Value, rows CFG, COLS and DATA, each JSON with a leading | (so Sheets never reads it as a number or formula), a long value continued on the next rows under the same key. DATA explains itself in its ABOUT entry. In public-comment mode it holds SECTIONS (each section the comments can name: key → [name shown, PDF page]), ABBREVIATIONS (short names such as HWR → a section key), PAGE_LINES ([PDF page, first line, last line]), PAGE_OFFSET (PDF page = printed page + this) and LAST_PAGE. In drafting mode it holds TOC (the dropdown: [name shown, anchor]). The script also reads the short names K, ABBR, LP, OFFSET and MAX. # the script, once per platform version bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/build-review-sheet-script.ts --script Code.gs . # one document's Config rows, from the folio's repository root bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/build-review-sheet-script.ts \ --repo . --config review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json --out config-rows.json . A drafting sheet also gets its TOC tab (the Selected Sections dropdown): . bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/build-review-sheet-script.ts \ --repo . --config review/drafting/sheet-sync.json --out config-rows.json --toc-out toc-rows.json . The agent writes config-rows.json into the Config tab (A1 down, columns A and B, clearing rows below) with the Sheets connector, which runs as the owner, and keeps the tab protected so only the owner can edit it. CFG and COLS, which a person might edit by hand, are indented JSON cut into cells between lines, and column B wraps; DATA, generated from the folio, stays compact. The script joins a key’s cells and parses them. Neither file is committed: both are rebuilt. Install it, once per sheet, from the sheet owner’s account, because Google asks the owner to authorise the script: §”Installing the script, step by step” below. installTriggers runs a full refresh, then installs two triggers: every edit of the three tabs marks the sheet dirty, and every minute a dirty sheet is rebuilt. The agent writes the Agent tab through the API, which fires no edit, so the timer also rebuilds after an Agent change: . | Drafting sheets rebuild incrementally. An edit rebuilds only the rows it touched, at once, so a pick shows its link and a new row its Change-set within seconds. The timer rebuilds only the rows whose change set’s Agent row changed (the script keeps a short hash per change set). A new table of contents in Config, an edit of the header row, or Refresh now rebuilds everything. | Public-comment sheets rebuild whole, since a comment feeds its change sets: at once while a rebuild takes under 5 s, otherwise gathered for the timer, which also rebuilds when the Agent tab changed since the last rebuild. On a sheet too slow to rebuild per edit, an edit of Review Change Sets still flags a stale proposal at once (staleNow, reading only that tab and the agent’s change-set tab). | . Folio Assistant → Refresh now rebuilds at once. Stale staging previews. The agent records when it built a change set’s preview in the Agent tab’s Staging built (UTC, change set), beside Agent completed (UTC, change set). When a PR of the change set was completed after the build, the script writes the Staging review cell as review ⚠ stale: built <time>, PR changed since, in both modes (Review Change Sets takes the link from the Agent tab’s Staging review page (change set) where it names one). Without a build time it claims nothing. The preview page shows its own live banner too (the site’s staging build, cat-harness-tools). Checked by commit. Times can agree while the preview is still wrong, so the agent also records, on each pass over a change set with an open PR: . | Agent tab column | what the agent writes | where it reads it | . | PR head (change set) | each PR’s latest commit, one per line, in the PR order | the PR (gh pr view --json headRefOid) | . | Staging built from (change set) | the commit the preview was built from | the newest gh-pages commit touching branches/<slug>/. Its message is staging(<slug>): from <sha> when an agent staged it (stage-local.ts), or Publish <site> <sha8> preview of <branch> when the site-publish workflow did; both forms are accepted | . | Staging deploy (change set) | the restage’s stage, updated as it moves: building (the site is being built), pushed (on gh-pages, waiting for Pages), deploying (Pages is deploying it; pending reads the same), deployed, or failed | the Pages deployment of that gh-pages commit: gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pages/builds/latest, or, where that endpoint is blocked, the conclusion of the “pages build and deployment” run in actions/runs?head_sha=<gh-pages commit> | . On every push, in the same pass: write the new PR head, set Staging deploy to building, set each comment’s status, and stamp Agent completed with the clock (date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%MZ'), never an estimate. A push recorded only in prose leaves the sheet saying the old preview is current and the row is “Not started”. Then, as the restage moves: on the gh-pages push, write Staging built from and Staging built and set pushed; when the Pages run starts, deploying; when it succeeds, deployed. The sheet shows each stage in Staging review and the ⏳ line. With each stage before deployed the agent adds when it expects the preview live, from the clock and recent runs of the same site (gh run list --workflow pages-build-deployment and the build’s own duration): building, expected 2026-10-31 15:20Z. The sheet shows “expected live " after the stage. Writing the Agent tab with the tool . The agent does not type numbers or times into the Agent tab: a tool makes the cells, and the agent runs the sheet’s own check before writing. | Dispositions. Read Agent - Comments (No., Change-sets) and Review Public Comments (No., Disposition) with their header rows, and the change set’s current Disposition (change set) cell. Put them in an input file with the items (which numbers, which word, why; rest for “every other comment of the change set”), and run bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/agent-record.ts dispositions <input.json>. The tool takes the change set’s numbers from the sheet, groups them (Nos. 127 to 131, 134, 135, 138 and 139), uses the people’s Blue word where an item names none, keeps every earlier Decided line, and runs dispositionProblems from the same review-sheet.gs the sheet runs. If anything would show a ⚠, it prints the problems, exits 1 and writes nothing: fix the input and run it again. Write its output, unchanged, to Disposition (change set). | On every push. agent-record.ts push --head <full sha> --expect <minutes> prints PR head, Staging deploy (building, expected <time>) and Agent completed, the times from the clock. Write all three in one update. | After acting on Ready for agent with no new commit (the PR already held the change), run agent-record.ts done and write the Agent completed it prints, so it is later than the Ready time and the ⏳ line moves on. Not push: nothing is restaged, so Staging deploy stays as it is. | When the QA gate passes, run agent-record.ts qa-pass --cs <CS-nnn> --head <sha> --summary "<one line>" --report <url> (or pass --qa-gate "Passed <sha>: <one line>" and optional --blocks <b1,b2> / --since <ref>). It checks the gate string with the sheet’s own qaGate and writes one editing-hci-validation workflow instance (beans/workflows/editing--<block>.json) per changed block, advancing through Task_Commit with the change-set id, the Passed <sha> QA review and the editor’s review-sheet decision, so check:corpus-gate goes green. | The PR’s review brief. agent-record.ts brief <input.json> --look "<where to look>" prints the same Overall and per-comment lines as Markdown between <!-- review-brief --> and <!-- /review-brief -->. Put it in the PR body: the staging review page’s “What to expect in this review” pane shows only that section. Add --pcs <public-comment dashboard url> (on smart-ra, https://litlfred.github.io/smart-ra/en/folio-assistant-core/public-comments/folio/dpi-h-ra/) and every comment number links to its row there. The link target is the comment’s own id from the Agent - Comments “Comment ref” column (pass those rows as comments): the sheet’s No. is not the id (on DPI-H, No. 136 is PC-0137). A run such as “127 to 131” is spelled out, so no comment hides behind a range. | Each move. agent-record.ts step <name> (§”Where the agent is: Agent step”). | . Drafting sheets have no comment numbers: pass "nos": []; the tool then only keeps the history. The script compares only; it stays @OnlyCurrentDoc with no internet access. Short and full shas both work: it compares the common prefix, at least 7 characters. It reads the active PR as the last one listed (one branch, one active PR per row) and writes, in this order of precedence: ⚠ deploy failed; ⚠ stale: built from <sha>, PR now at <sha> (with ; restaging: <stage> while one runs); ⚠ restaging: building the preview | on gh-pages, waiting for Pages to deploy | Pages is deploying it. A change set with a recorded PR head but no preview link shows ⚠ no preview yet: not ready for merge. A change set is never ready for merge without a preview to review: the agent stages a preview for every PR it opens, and the “Merge decision due” filter view leaves out rows whose Staging review starts with ⚠. Without these columns the script falls back to the time check above. It finds them by header, so on a sheet that lacks them the agent adds them at the right of the Agent (change sets) tab. Ready for agent after the preview. The PR has not changed yet when an Editor sends a row back, so the commit check above passes. The script records, as a document property ready:<CS>, the time it first sees a row’s Ready for agent at Yes (cleared on No). A Yes it first sees on a row the agent has already completed counts from that completion instead, since the script cannot know when it was set. When that time is later than Staging built, after the deploy checks, it writes ⚠ missing feedback from <time>: the preview still shows the PR, but not the feedback an Editor has just sent to the agent. Only the sheet says so; the review page cannot know the sheet. The same time makes Agentic status open with **Waiting on the agent since (Ready for agent set)**, until the agent records a later completion or sets the status to Working. Stale agent proposals. Feedback (agent) (drafting) and Change Set Feedback (agent) (Review Change Sets) carry the agent’s proposal. The agent records what it wrote against in the Agent tab’s Feedback basis (change set): feedbackBasis() in tools/review-sheet-sync/feedback-issue.ts, a hash of the row’s blue cells (drafting: Title, Selected Sections, people’s Contributor Feedback; public comment: Title, TWG (CS), people’s Committee Feedback). The script computes the same hash; while they differ it puts “⚠ Stale: the row changed since this proposal; the agent will propose again.” on the proposal’s first line, and takes it off if the row changes back. The agent’s next sync replaces the proposal and the basis. In a public-comment sheet the agent writes a 2: basis: feedbackBasis(header, row, ["Title", "TWG (CS)"], "Committee Feedback", PC_BASIS_GREY). It also covers the grey content Review Change Sets joins from the change set’s comments (Sections, Pages, Public Comments, Suggested Revisions, PC Committee Feedback, Dispositions, TWG (PCs)), so a proposal goes stale when a comment it rests on changes, not only when a blue cell on its own row does. The agent’s own columns (Agentic status, Staging review page, the proposal) are never part of it, so the agent’s writes never make its own proposals stale. A stored basis without 2: is compared with the blue-only hash, so a sheet moves over one row at a time as the agent rewrites each basis. Where the change set is. Below any stale mark, the script keeps one bold line starting with ⏳ at the top of the agent’s proposal (progressLine, withProgress), and replaces it on every refresh: “Ready for merge set: the agent will merge dth-hrh#7.”; “Ready for agent set <time>: the agent will act on this and rewrite it.”; “The agent is working on dth-hrh#7.”; or “dth-hrh#7 open; no preview yet | preview current (built <time>) | preview missing feedback from <time>.” An open PR’s line carries the agent’s last completion time (“smart-ra#185 open, updated 2026-10-31 14:41Z; preview stale: built from 420acd3, PR now at e7b4094.”). No pull request, a merged one, or an empty proposal gets no line. The agent never writes this line or any status line of its own, and drops it when it rewrites the proposal; the next refresh (within a minute) puts it back. The agent records the facts in the Agent tab (PR head, Staging deploy, Agent completed from date -u) and the sheet says them. An Editor’s Orange change (a Ready column) is not part of the basis, so it never marks the proposal stale: it shows here as a note, and Ready stays as the Editor set it. The note appears at once: an edit of a Ready for agent cell records its time (noteReady_) and, on a slow public-comment sheet, staleNow writes that row’s line without waiting for the timer. How to tell it works. The first run of installTriggers takes about 20 seconds for 800 rows and its execution log ends “Execution completed” (a one-second run means onOpen was picked). Then No. is a blue link, and hovering a No. n on Review Change Sets shows a row such as A327. Failed runs are listed with their error under Executions (the clock icon) in the Apps Script editor. An agent checks from outside by reading a No. cell’s formula (=HYPERLINK(…)) and a joined cell’s text-format runs. Protected columns. The script runs as the account that installed it, so it writes the grey and green columns even when they are protected, as long as that account is an editor of the protected ranges. Install it from the owner’s account. Reuse it for another document’s public comment. Nothing in the template names a document. Give the new folio: . | The frozen review version in library/<slug>/, with its pdf-line-map.json, and the folio’s review-anchors.json (the extraction described in public-comment §”The one fact everything rests on” makes both). | A draft/ redirect on its site to the library viewer, or use the full viewer address as draftUrl. | review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json: . { "anchors": "folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json", "lineMap": "library/<slug>/pdf-line-map.json", "draftUrl": "draft/#page=", "commentUrl": "en/folio-assistant-core/public-comments/folio/<doc>/index.html#", "namedSections": { "CR": "Client Registry" }, "aliases": { "how to use the guidance": "How to use this guidance" }, "tabs": { "RPC": "Review Public Comments" }, "columns": { "rpc": { "lines": "Line no(s) / Table / Figure" } } } . namedSections lists the unnumbered sections reviewers cite by name, and their abbreviations, which are matched only in capitals. aliases gives other names for front-matter chapters. tabs and columns override the defaults in build-review-sheet-script.ts only where the new sheet’s headers differ. The printed-to-PDF offset and the last printed page are read from the line map. | A sheet with the tabs above, Agent’s No., Comment ref and Change-sets columns filled, then build and install as above. | . Test it without a sheet. bun test folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/review-sheet.test.ts builds the script for a small fake folio and runs it against a fake of the Apps Script services over the three tabs. It checks every link and join in the table above, the Agentic status lines, and the edit-and-timer refresh. It does not prove a given sheet has the script installed or current: that is How to tell it works. Change the template, the builder or this table only together with that test. Rewrite the Config tab when the review anchors change, the draft link moves, or a tab or a header the script reads is renamed. Re-paste Code.gs only when the script itself changes. Renaming a header the script reads, without rewriting Config, leaves that column unlinked; it fails nothing.

3224.title: Ready for agent: Yes, No, Completed
3224.content: The script sets Ready for agent from Yes to Completed once the agent’s last push is later than the time Yes was set and the preview of it is live and current (no ⚠ in Staging review). An Editor sets Yes again to send the row back to the agent. A row that turns stale goes back to No from Yes or Completed. The agent never writes the Orange columns. Every pass ends with a finish stamp after the Ready time: . | The agent ends EVERY pass with a stamp from the tool: push --head <sha> when it committed, else done, which writes Agent completed and the step idle together. A proposal that waits for the Editor ends with step proposed. The script counts a later idle or proposed step as the end of the pass, the same as Agent completed. | Before stopping, the agent re-reads Ready for agent: if it was set after the pass began, the pass is not over; act on it (or done if there is nothing new). | A Ready for agent with no step recorded after it for 20 minutes shows “⚠ no agent has picked this up for N min: ask in the project chat” on the ⏳ line and in Agentic status, so a row with no agent never looks like quiet work. | Every log needs a watcher: the setup is not complete until an agent thread is watching the sheet. A thread acts only when something wakes it, so the watcher needs a scheduled wake: an hourly scheduled task, plus a chain of 3-minute delayed wakes (send_later) that each pass renews. Each wake runs the mechanical check of skill review-log-watch first, and does agent work only when it reports a change. For that check the script writes, in a drafting sheet, a hash of every cell people set on Contributor Feedback to the hidden Watch tab (F1:I1: Cells hash, the hash, Checked (UTC), the time), on every refresh and timer tick. In a public-comment sheet it covers Review Change Sets (Title, TWG (CS), every Committee Feedback column, Ready for agent, Dispositions confirmed, Ready for merge, Change Set (human)) and Review Public Comments (every Committee Feedback column, Disposition, Change Set (human), TWG (human)), keyed by Change-set id and comment No., so an inserted row changes nothing; it is written on every refresh, which the timer runs only when an edit or the Agent tab changed. Without a watcher, a Ready for agent waits until somebody happens to ask. | .

3225.title: One agent column, status on top
3225.content: A sheet without an Agentic status column gets the status on top of the agent column (Change Set Feedback (agent) or Feedback (agent)) instead: . ⏳ smart-ra#185 open, updated 2026-10-31 15:26Z; preview current (built 15:19Z). ↳ smart-ra#185 (PR open, 2026-10-31 15:26Z) · DPI-F at first use <the agent's proposal and any Decision needed question> . The ⏳ line and each ↳ line (one per pull request, linked; and the ask when people must answer) are the script’s; it replaces them on every refresh and never stacks them. The agent writes only what is below them and never starts its own text with ⏳ or ↳. Agentic status (filter) stays, for the filter views. A sheet that keeps its Agentic status column keeps the status there; delete that column to switch.

3226.title: The QA gate, before Ready for merge
3226.content: Who. A reviewer that did not write the change: another agent session, or a person. The authoring agent never gates its own pull request. What it checks, against the PR’s head commit: . | every comment (drafting: every feedback item) of the change set has one disposition (the script’s dispositionProblems already flags gaps); | each disposition agrees with the people’s Blue Disposition, where one is set; | each Accepted or Partially accepted item has its change in the PR’s diff, and the change does what the line says; | a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope item has no change in the diff that contradicts it; | the diff changes nothing that no disposition accounts for; | the staging QA report for that commit has no failing gate. | . What it writes, on the Agent tab’s change-set row and nowhere else: . | QA gate (change set): first line Passed <head sha>: <one line> or Failed <head sha>: <the first problem>, then one line per problem; | QA report (change set): the link to the QA report for the staged commit: the tree pr/<n>/<sha> on the folio’s QA reports branch (in smart-ra, cat/cat-harness/qa-reports; check the branch name, it varies). | . When the gate passes, run agent-record.ts qa-pass (§”Writing the Agent tab with the tool”). What the sheet shows. Staging review reads review · QA report (both links), then the gate: ✓ QA gate passed (b20534f), or in bold ⚠ QA gate: no independent review yet: not ready for merge, ⚠ QA gate failed: <why>, or ⚠ QA gate stale: reviewed 1234567, PR now at b20534f: not ready for merge once the PR moves on (qaGate). If Ready for merge is set before the gate passes, the agent’s ⏳ line says it will not merge until it does, and the agent does not merge. A failed gate sends the change set back to the author, who updates the PR and its dispositions; the gate then runs again on the new head.

3227.title: Unconfirmed dispositions block the merge
3227.content: The agent’s disposition for a comment is a proposal until the committee records its own word in the people’s Disposition column. While any comment of a change set is still Pending (or empty) there, Disposition (agent) shows “⚠ Not confirmed by the committee (Disposition still Pending): Nos. …”. Staging review shows “⚠ dispositions not complete or not confirmed: not ready for merge”, and the ⏳ line says the agent will not merge until every disposition is complete and confirmed. The agent never merges such a change set, even with Ready for merge = Yes. agent-record.ts dispositions does not stop on this line, because confirming is the committee’s step, not a fault in the agent’s record. An Editor confirms in the Orange Dispositions confirmed column, left of Ready for merge. There are only three ways to confirm, and no per-comment checkbox: . | Yes confirms every agent disposition in the change set; | comment numbers typed in the cell (“No. 327”) confirm just those; a number outside the change set is flagged; | to differ on one comment, the committee sets that comment’s own Disposition on Review Public Comments, and a mismatch is flagged. | . The script adds the column itself, inside its locked run (so no other refresh writes by a shifted position), and keeps its Yes/No dropdown.

3228.title: Where the agent is: Agent step
3228.content: At every move the agent writes Agent step (change set) on its change-set tab, with agent-record.ts step <name> so the time comes from the clock. The script shows it on the ⏳ line for as long as it holds, e.g. “⏳ Agent: editing the document (since today 17:20Z)” (or “yesterday …”, or “3 days ago, 2026-10-28 …”), and adds “⚠ no update for N min” after 30 minutes. A question for a person (“Needs you: answer the Decision needed below, then set Ready for agent to Yes”) always comes first. The script adds the column, at the end of the tab, inside its locked run. | step | when the agent writes it | BPMN task | . | reading | it starts on new feedback or a Ready for agent | (start of Task_Propose / Task_EditInPullRequest; public comment: Task_AuthorEdits) | . | proposing | it writes or rewrites its proposal | Task_Propose (public comment: Task_ProposeChangeSets) | . | editing | it edits the document on the branch | Task_EditInPullRequest (Task_AuthorEdits) | . | pushing | it commits and pushes | end of the edit task, with push | . | staging | the preview is building | the staging step of the edit task | . | deploying | Pages is publishing the preview | as above | . | qa-review | it waits for the independent reviewer | Task_QaGate | . | merging | it merges after Ready for merge | Task_Merge (Task_Incorporate) | . | proposed | it has written a proposal and waits for Ready for agent = Yes; the ⏳ line says “Proposal ready: set Ready for agent to Yes” | end of Task_Propose | . | idle | it stops: done, or waiting on a person | — | . The agent writes its proposal straight into the feedback cell, which drops the ⏳ line; the timer watches that column (without the script’s own lines), so the status comes back on the next tick without anyone pressing Refresh. Write idle (or the next step) before leaving a change set; a step left behind turns into the “no update” warning.

3229.title: Rows at most 10 lines high
3229.content: Sheets cannot scroll inside a cell, so on the people’s tabs (Review Public Comments, Review Change Sets, Contributor Feedback) a row whose text would run past about 10 lines is fixed at that height and the rest is clipped. Clicking the cell shows the whole text in the formula bar, and double-clicking opens it scrollable. Rows that fit size themselves, and a row that shrinks back under the cap is released. The script estimates lines from column widths (capRows), so it needs no layout access.

3230.title: Structured cells and column hover text
3230.content: A list is never run together with semicolons. Agents write “What changed” and “What the PRs changed (change set)” one item per line, as • <item> (No. n), under a label line ending in a colon. The script splits any remaining a; b; c into bullet lines, and bolds line-start labels (What changed:, Proposed direction:) and comment references (No. 326, Nos. 1, 2 and 5). Every column head carries a hover note saying what the column holds and who fills it in, without naming its colour. The notes are HEADER_NOTES in the script, keyed by header (or <tab kind>|<header> where one header means different things on different tabs); a head named Name (initials) uses its Name (*) entry. The script owns the note on every head it knows and writes only notes that changed; a head it does not know keeps its own. A new column gets its note in the same change that adds its header; review-sheet.test.ts checks that every known head has one and that none names a colour. The QA report link opens the viewer, the preview review page’s per-section QA table (<review page>#heat), with the raw qa-reports entry beside it as “files”. Text in a cell that is not a link is written plain, so it never inherits a link’s blue underline.

3231.title: Sheet conventions (any agent-written Google Sheet)
3231.content: These hold for every Google Sheet an agent writes or keeps current, not only the review sheets: . | colour | who controls it | lock | . | grey | mechanical: ids, headers, copied source text | owner only | . | blue | people: the human-controlled columns | open to the sheet’s editors | . | orange | editor gates (Ready for agent, Ready for merge) | its own lock, owner plus the named editors | . | green | agent-derived: links, joins, status | owner only | . | Templates are locked to the owner except the blue columns; the orange gates carry their own lock that starts with the owner alone. | The Config tab is visible, never hidden, and locked to the owner: the agent writes it, people can read what the sheet is set up for. | Instructions name no colour. The key on the first line reads “Column colours:” then one phrase per colour (“your input, by …”, “written by the agent”, …), each shown in its colour, and the steps name columns (“Reviewers update Contributor Feedback”, “an Editor sets Ready for agent”), never a colour. The script’s colourInstructions shows each column name bold in a darker shade of that column’s header fill, on every refresh, so text the agent rewrites through the API, which drops the colours, gets them back within a minute. | Which template depends on the document’s authoring stage: the Contributor template while it is being drafted and authored, the Public Comment Review template once public comment opens. | .

3232.title: Published with the document’s site
3232.content: scripts/review-sheet-site.ts --out <site> (package script site:review-sheet in a folio, a sourceSteps entry of its site build) writes <site>/review-sheet/: the generic Code.gs, each review/<mode>/sheet-sync.json as <mode>.config-rows.json, review-sheet.jsonld (the script as schema:SoftwareSourceCode with its SHA-256 and commit; each document’s settings as a schema:Dataset linked to its sheet and to the Tool), and an index.html with the setup steps and the SHA-256 to check a pasted copy against. Point people there rather than sending the file.

3233.title: Trusting the script
3233.content: A copy of a sheet carries its Apps Script, so anyone starting from a template should know what they are running. | Nothing runs until the sheet’s owner allows it. The owner runs installTriggers; Google then shows the scopes, and the triggers run as the owner, whoever’s edit fires them. So an editor’s edit makes owner code read what they typed: the script therefore never writes typed text as a formula (asText, q), and touches only this sheet. | Security review. tools/review-sheet-sync/security-review.md records the threat model and findings F1 to F10, each fixed with a test or accepted with its reason. Re-review on any new write sink, service, or editor-writable tab. | The agent caps new issues (finding F6): it opens a change set’s issue only for a row with a Title or feedback text, and asks a person before opening more than 20 in one sync. | This sheet only. The template starts with @OnlyCurrentDoc, so the consent screen asks for “this spreadsheet”, not all of the owner’s spreadsheets. The script uses only SpreadsheetApp, PropertiesService, LockService and ScriptApp: no UrlFetchApp, mail or Drive, so it sends nothing out. review-sheet-security.test.ts fails if one of those, or eval/new Function, appears. | Three permissions, one file. Google works out a script’s permissions from its code, and @OnlyCurrentDoc narrows the spreadsheet one to this sheet. So the consent screen asks for exactly three: this spreadsheet, the script’s own triggers, and its menu. tools/review-sheet-sync/appsscript.json records those three for the security test, which fails if the code would need more. It is a record, not a file to paste. | Plain ASCII. The built script escapes every non-ASCII character, so a paste cannot mangle it. The build prints its SHA-256; compare it with the pasted copy. | Wrong sheet. Pasted into a sheet it was not built for, it stops with a message naming the config and tab it expected, before installing triggers. | Check a copy against its source. The script is the same for every document, so one review covers all copies. Its header names the folio-assistant-core commit it was built from. Build again at that commit with the folio’s config and compare; or ignore the copied script and paste one you built yourself. | “Google hasn’t verified this app.” Bound scripts are unverified, so the owner clicks Advanced to continue. Publishing as a verified Workspace add-on would remove the warning. | .

3234.title: Drafting mode: editors’ and contributors’ feedback
3234.content: Before a document goes to public comment, editors and contributors give feedback on the working draft. That needs a simpler sheet: no Public Comment Source, no Review Public Comments, no TWGs. Each row of feedback is a change set (CS: a list of related comments on one topic), and each change set gets a GitHub issue. Tabs. | tab | who writes | columns | . | Contributor Feedback | people, plus the Apps Script | one row per change set. Grey, mechanical: Change-set (the script gives a used row the next CS-nnn once; it stays with the row). Blue, people: Title; Selected Sections (a multi-select dropdown of the document’s table of contents, each section indented under its chapter by three U+2800 blanks per level, since a dropdown cannot nest; not real spaces, because Sheets trims a multi-select cell and the first chip would lose them and read as Invalid; plain, because a dropdown chip cannot carry a link); any number of Contributor Feedback (…) columns, one per contributor, with their initials or name in the brackets (e.g. Contributor Feedback (CL); the script reads every column whose header is Contributor Feedback or starts Contributor Feedback (); Disposition (a dropdown: Pending, Accepted, Partially accepted, Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate, Out of scope), the committee’s verdict on the row. Orange, editors: Ready for agent (Yes, No, Completed), Ready for merge (Yes/No). Grey, by the script: Section links (each selected section on its own line, linked to its place on the document page, like the Sections column of the public-comment log). Green, by the agent: Feedback (agent), right of Ready for merge, the agent’s proposed direction (not a person’s feedback: the script leaves it out of the Contributor Feedback columns, and it decides nothing). Green, by the script from Agent: Issue (<repo>#n, linked), Agentic status (as in public-comment mode: one line per PR, <repo>#n (status, completed) · what it changed), Staging review (a “review” link to the change set’s review page on its staging preview, branches/<branch>/en/review/, while its PR is open), Agentic status (filter) (the change set’s status as one plain value, for the “By agentic status” filter view) | . | Agent | the agent only | one row per change set: Change-set, Issue (URL), Agentic status, Pull request (change set), What the PRs changed (change set), Agent completed (UTC, change set), Staging review page (change set), Feedback basis (change set). The agent writes it as each step completes, by the steps of the review-sheet-agent-columns skill; a drafting sheet has no per-comment rows, so only its change-set columns apply | . | TOC (hidden) | the script | the Sections dropdown’s list and each entry’s link. Rewritten on every refresh, so it follows the document | . Colours as in public-comment mode: grey mechanical, blue human, orange editor gates, green agent-derived. Built from the folio’s review-anchors.json: each chapter (Ch 3 Digital Transformation Approach), each numbered section (3.1 DIIG alignment) and each unnumbered section, prefixed by its chapter (Ch 3 · Objectives and key messages). A multi-select cell joins its choices with , , so commas in titles become ;. Each links to sectionUrl + the anchor (sec:3-1, chap:<dir>), which the document page carries as element ids. Config, review/drafting/sheet-sync.json: . { "mode": "drafting", "anchors": "folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json", "sectionUrl": "en/<doc>/#" } . Write the URLs relative to the folio’s site: the build resolves them against iriBase in the folio’s <instance>.json (e.g. https://litlfred.github.io/dth-hrh/), so no organisation name is written in sheet-sync.json and a folio that moves changes one iriBase and rewrites its Config. An absolute https:// URL is taken as written. tabs and columns (draft, draftAgent) override the headers as in public-comment mode. Write its Config with --config review/drafting/sheet-sync.json and install as above. The Sections dropdown is a data validation “dropdown from a range” on TOC!A2:A with Allow multiple selections ticked (step 6 below). Without the tick, a cell with two or more sections shows “Invalid: Input must fall within specified range”. The agent’s part: every change set has an issue. On each sync, for every Contributor Feedback row with a Change-set: . | If the Agent tab has no row for it, add one (Change-set, Agentic status Not started). | If that row has no Issue, open a GitHub issue in the folio’s repository: title CS-nnn: <Title> (or the first feedback line while Title is empty), body the linked sections, every Contributor Feedback (…) cell verbatim, and a link back to the sheet row. Write its URL into Issue. | When feedback is added to a row later, comment the new text on its issue. | Propose a direction in Feedback (agent) for every new row (from an issue, a person or a TWG workbook) and whenever the row changes, whoever changed it. The watcher does this on its next wake (skill review-log-watch, step 5). A question for people goes there too, as a Decision needed: block (§”Inputs and outputs”). On each sync compute feedbackBasis(header, row) (tools/review-sheet-sync/feedback-issue.ts: a short hash of Title, Selected Sections and the people’s Contributor Feedback columns). Where it differs from the Agent tab’s Feedback basis (change set), or the proposal cell is empty (a person clears it to ask for a fresh one), write a new proposal and the new basis. The script’s own writes (ids, links, tree marks) do not change the basis. | Work a change set only when Ready for agent is Yes; its PRs say Closes #n for the change set’s issue, and go to Agent’s PR columns. | When you pick a row up, say so first: set its Agent status to Working and put the URL of your conversation (the session, thread or PR discussion) in Agent conversation (change set). Agentic status then opens with An agent is working on it: conversation, linked. The script finds that column by header; on a sheet that lacks it, the agent adds it at the right of the Agent (change sets) tab. | . Title is the people’s on both kinds of sheet: the agent never writes it. In public-comment mode a Title-only row on Review Change Sets is a new change set, and the agent’s title is only the first value of a row it adds (skill review-log-watch, “Change sets people make”). Feedback from the site.
